name: sands-of-the-restless
description: A browser FPS built in a weekend. Three.js, no build step, everything generated in code.

scripts._comment:kite: test/kite.mjs is DELIBERATELY OUT of `npm test`. It drives three thousand real requestAnimationFrame frames through the real main loop, which under swiftshader is half an hour, and a half-hour gate in a twenty-four suite run is a gate nobody runs. It is the played verification of the Act 2 route and it is run on purpose.
scripts._comment:e2e: test/e2e.mjs is DELIBERATELY OUT of `npm test`, for the same reason kite is: it plays all twenty-five waves. It is the ONLY harness that climbs the wave ladder instead of setting it - it replaces director.forceWave and director.reset with functions that record a violation and throw, so the shortcut is mechanically unavailable rather than merely unused. test/jars.mjs proves every part of the ending and reaches wave 25 with forceWave; this proves the ladder underneath it. Run it before shipping World 1, and after any change to the director's wave or phase machinery.
scripts._comment:stuck: THREE HARNESSES, AND THE ORDER MATTERS. test/stuck.mjs sweeps the quarry and the canal on a grid and reports places the body cannot walk out of - it is a CANDIDATE finder and its output is not a bug list. test/stuck-trap.mjs is the one that decides: it walks AT each candidate from open ground and then tries to walk back out, because the inside of a rock face is a place you cannot walk out of and it is not a defect. Only a place you can get INTO and not out of is a bug. test/stuck-pins.mjs re-walks a fixed coordinate list on real frames and is the A/B instrument: the sweep cannot compare a fix to a baseline because its own clustering picks the points, so a run reporting different coordinates before and after has measured two different things. All three are OUT of `npm test` - they are minutes each, and the trap test is the only one whose verdict should ever be quoted.
scripts._comment:solid: test/solid.mjs proves the horde is SOLID, and it runs its own control: every case is walked twice, once with player.setBodies(null) - the behaviour that shipped until 2026-08-03 - and once with the horde wired in. A harness that reports "solid" without ever having seen "not solid" has not shown it can tell the difference. It is out of `npm test` because it is minutes of real frames, and it must be run after any change to resolveCollisions, to the actor death path, or to attackRange - contact damage fires at 2.57 m and the body stops at 0.78 m, and a change that closes that gap turns a fix into a different bug.
